'''2000 Decipher World Championship''' was the fifth Star Wars CCG World Championship, played 5–7 October 2000 at [[DecipherCon 2000]] in the Doubletree Resort and Conference Center, Kissimmee, Florida. [[Matt Sokol]] (United States) defeated [[Yannick Lapointe]] (Canada) in the Final Confrontation.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016121021/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="sokol">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], [[Trandosite]] (25 October 2000)</ref><ref name="sched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20061009205800/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/schedule/ DecipherCon 2000 schedule], Decipher (Wayback 9 October 2006)</ref>

[[File:DecipherCon 2000 SWCCG champion plaque.jpg|thumb|right|280px|2000 World Champion plaque]]
[[File:DecipherCon 2000 tournament hall.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Main hall, 6 October 2000]]

[[Trandosite]] called the weekend the largest World Championship field to that date.<ref name="trando-wf">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050517110350/http://trandosite.mcmail.com/wf00p2.htm History of the World Finals], [[Trandosite]]</ref> The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Death Star II]]. [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] had been published on 19 July 2000. It covers the Battle of Endor and the second Death Star.<ref name="ds2">[[Death Star II (expansion)]]</ref>

This was the last Star Wars Worlds Decipher ran at a company convention. On 3 October 2001 [[Warren Holland]] cancelled [[DecipherCon 2001]].<ref name="holland">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Special_message_from_Decipher_CEO_Warren_Holland_70685.asp Special message from Decipher CEO Warren Holland], TheForce.Net (3 October 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010073714/https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Special_message_from_Decipher_CEO_Warren_Holland_70685.asp Internet Archive]</ref>

== Format ==

* '''Environment:''' [[Premiere - Death Star II]]
* '''Site:''' [[DecipherCon 2000]], Doubletree Resort and Conference Center, Kissimmee, Florida
* '''Dates:''' 5–7 October 2000 (Thursday–Saturday); the convention continued through 8 October
* '''Field:''' Day 1 open, about 170 (Lalumiere, Guzman, Faust); Wikipedia and ''Insider'' 52 give 72. Day 2: 70 World Finalists (32 circuit + 38 wildcards); 57 with posted Final Totals (Decipher results page)<ref name="wp" /><ref name="insider">''Star Wars Insider'' 52 (2000)</ref><ref name="fkl2">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010107221700/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/fkl2.html Mighty Jabba Sails Across the Atlantic], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher (Wayback 7 January 2001)</ref><ref name="guzman-d1">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-10-info-brokers-dcon-day-one-reportd1317/ info-brokers-dcon-day-one-report], Tim Guzman, Decktech (10 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024003601/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-10-info-brokers-dcon-day-one-reportd1317/ Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="d2">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001026043505/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/starwars.html DecipherCon 2000 Day 2]</ref><ref name="tr-d1335" /><ref name="dc00fin" />

[[Justin Pakes]] directed the Star Wars rooms.<ref name="tennet">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cardsd1338/ deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cards], Alex "Greedo" Tennet, Decktech (13 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008203411/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cardsd1338/ Internet Archive]</ref> Day 1 was eight games. The top 38 joined pre-qualified champions on Day 2.<ref name="dc00fin">[http://decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swfinalists.html DecipherCon 2000: Star Wars CCG Qualifiers], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010308110320/http://decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swfinalists.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="guzman-d1" /> Day 2 was eight games (4 Light / 4 Dark). Twelve advanced to Day 3. Day 3 reset those twelve for four games (2 Light / 2 Dark). The top two played the Final Confrontation.<ref name="d3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010303120030/http://decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/starwars3.html DecipherCon 2000 Day 3]</ref>

The last Day 2 slot was [[Dominic Gaudreault]] 10 (+70). [[Martin Akesson]] 10 (+69) missed by one differential.<ref name="d2" /> On Day 3, [[Kevin Shannon]]'s Game 2 Dark vs [[Steve Brentson]] was a '''Modified Win by 14''' (+1 victory point). A full win there would have moved Shannon past Sokol on the cut math. That example is on [[Tournaments#2000 World Championship — Sokol, Shannon, and a modified win]].<ref name="d3" />

== Qualifiers ==
32 players automatically qualified for Day 2 of the World Championship, skipping Day 1. These included the 1999 champion [[Gary Carman]], 4 Open champions, 3 Continental champions, and 24 Regional champions. Decipher published the seats as 1 defending champion + 4 Open + 3 Continental + 24 Regional + 38 wildcards = 70 World Finalists. The 70-player Day 2 field and the 38 wildcard seats were both set before the weekend.<ref name="dc00fin" />

The Coruscant regional had co-champions: [[John Lolli]] and [[Patrick Ziagos]]. Decipher listed both on the official qualifier list, so the named circuit list is 33 names for those 32 seats.<ref name="dc00fin" />

[[Bert-Olof Lundin]] is the Toola champion on Decipher's 2000 Regionals listing.<ref name="rl00toola">[http://christo.decipher.com/regionals/swlist.html?game=sw&region=toola 2000 Regionals: Toola], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010728171432/http://christo.decipher.com/regionals/swlist.html?game=sw&region=toola Internet Archive]</ref> The official Worlds qualifier list and Day 2 standings name [[Jesper Larsson]].<ref name="dc00fin" /><ref name="d2" /> [[Martin Akesson]] wrote that Larsson beat him in the Toola final. Larsson played Day 2.<ref name="tr-d1133">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-08-16-european-continentalsd1133/ european-continentals], DeckTech (Martin "Mart" Akesson, 16 August 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261025150849/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-08-16-european-continentalsd1133/ Internet Archive].</ref>

Any number of unqualified players could play in the Day 1 open for 38 wildcard seats in Day 2. Decipher representatives told the registration line, "don't worry everyone will get into the opens."<ref name="sokol-dt" /> Trandosite wrote that the wild card championship "throws the competition open to anyone."<ref name="trando-wf" /> Combined with the 32 qualifying players and the 38 wildcard seats would give a field of 70 total players for Day 2.

== Day 1 ==

Day 1 was the open wildcard. Unqualified players played eight games for 38 seats on Day 2.<ref name="dc00fin" /><ref name="guzman-d1" /> Play started hours late. Sokol wrote that the open began about 1 p.m., three hours after the posted time.<ref name="sokol-dt">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ sokols-dcon-2000-report], Matt Sokol, Decktech (11 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008202647/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ Internet Archive]</ref> [[John Arendt]] waited three hours past the published start.<ref name="arendt">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-09-deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2d1314/ deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2], John Arendt, Decktech (9 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024003721/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-09-deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2d1314/ Internet Archive]</ref> [[Hayes Hunter]] later said first pairings went up at 1 p.m. and the day ran until 2 a.m.<ref name="hayes-pds2-ops">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M&t=2794s SWCCG PDS2: Hayes Hunter Worlds 2023 Champion Interview], BillBisco2 (10 May 2025), 46:34–46:54. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-qJuistFFk9M Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010406/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 16 October 2026).</ref> [[Charlie Herren]] called Day 1 the most poorly run tournament he had seen.<ref name="herren" /> [[Paul Todd Feldman]] said the tournament software was not working properly and that pairings took a long time.<ref name="feldman-pds2-ops">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I&t=2428s SWCCG PDS2: Paul Todd Feldman Interview], BillBisco2 (29 May 2025), 40:28–40:37. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-b9f9tNBiU2I Internet Archive].</ref>

[[Peter Di Biasio]] went undefeated and won the Day 1 Swiss.<ref name="tennet" /><ref name="muller">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-10-05-00d1323/ 10-05-00], Brian Muller, Decktech (11 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024003906/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-10-05-00d1323/ Internet Archive]</ref> [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] finished second at 7–1.<ref name="winkelhaus-tr">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-deciphercon-by-bastian-winkelhausd1340/ deciphercon-by-bastian-winkelhaus], Bastian Winkelhaus, Decktech (14 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024004116/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-deciphercon-by-bastian-winkelhausd1340/ Internet Archive]</ref> [[Hayes Hunter]] finished third on Day 1.<ref name="hayes-tr">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-hayess-dcon-game-reportd1341/ hayess-dcon-game-report], Hayes Hunter, Decktech (14 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024004234/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-hayess-dcon-game-reportd1341/ Internet Archive]</ref> [[Dominic Gaudreault]] finished fourth.<ref name="dom">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-12-dom-goes-to-floridad1333/ dom-goes-to-florida], Dominic Gaudreault, Decktech (12 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009094534/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-12-dom-goes-to-floridad1333/ Internet Archive]</ref> [[Geoff Snider]] finished 12th and made the cut.<ref name="snider">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-08-deciphercon-2000d1309/ deciphercon-2000], Geoff Snider, Decktech (8 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024004439/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-08-deciphercon-2000d1309/ Internet Archive]</ref> Sokol finished 36th (Dark 4–0, Light 1–3).<ref name="sokol-dt" /> [[Tim Guzman]] finished 34th of the field he counted as 170.<ref name="guzman-d1" /> [[Brian Muller]] finished 29th at 5–3, 10 (+59).<ref name="muller" /> [[Gary Mohnsen]] took the last wildcard in a tie for 38th. [[Steven Turner]], [[Todd Rowe]], and [[Jim Sells]] made the cut with him.<ref name="muller" /> Brian Terwilliger wrote that [[Chris Terwilliger]] made Day 2.<ref name="twigg" /> Arendt named [[Kyle Craft]], [[Matt Berta]], and [[Chris Shaner]] among the Tatooine players on Day 2.<ref name="arendt" />

Sokol wrote: "Day 1 was the hardest tourney I have ever played in. It turns out that all the good players from around the world wanted to show up for this event."<ref name="sokol-dt" /> Arendt wrote that Day 1 competition was fierce because so many seats were open. He named the German crew, the Quebecers, and the Albany crew as the hard pockets.<ref name="arendt" /> [[Michael Fitzgerald]] called it "the biggest tournament of the year."<ref name="fitz">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-09-icemans-dcon-2000-reportd1310/ icemans-dcon-2000-report], Mike Fitzgerald, Decktech (9 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024004554/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-09-icemans-dcon-2000-reportd1310/ Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Disqualifications ===

Decipher deck-checked lists during the open. A list that did not match the 60-card deck ended the player's Worlds run.<ref name="tennet" /><ref name="sokol-dt" />

[[Jonny Chu]] was 5–2 going into game 8 when a check removed him. Sokol and [[Brian Terwilliger]] were at the table when the call came.<ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="tennet" /> Chu later said he had a 59-card list.<ref name="chu-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JLkMOP3rLQ8&t=1341s SWCCG PDS2: Jonny Chu Interview], BillBisco2 (28 April 2025), 22:21–22:49. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-JLkMOP3rLQ8 Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010509/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JLkMOP3rLQ8 watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 16 October 2026)</ref> [[Steven Lewis]] was 3–0 after game 3 when a check removed him.<ref name="lewis">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-15-how-to-get-disqualified-at-worldsd1349/ how-to-get-disqualified-at-worlds], Steven Lewis, Decktech (15 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024010428/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-15-how-to-get-disqualified-at-worldsd1349/ Internet Archive]</ref> Tennet also named [[Michael Girard]] and [[Kim Caton]] among the Day 1 disqualifications.<ref name="tennet" /> [[Michael Raveling]] was removed after game 5 for a 61-card list (Grey Squadron 1 written as Gold Squadron 1).<ref name="raveling">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-10-orlando-florida-2000d1318/ orlando-florida-2000], Michael Raveling, Decktech (10 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024004721/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-10-orlando-florida-2000d1318/ Internet Archive]</ref>

Players who missed the 38 included [[Alex Tennet]] (5–3), [[Justin Desai]] (5–3, about 41st), [[Charles Hickey]] (5–3, 10 (+20)), [[Jeff Anderson]] (86th on differential), [[Jeremy Oakes]] (100th), [[Joe Olson]], [[Joe Horbey]], [[Brian Terwilliger]], [[Chris Janiak]] (4–4), and [[Mike Kessling]].<ref name="tennet" /><ref name="desai">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-15-15-drunk-men-at-dennys-worldsd1346/ 15-drunk-men-at-dennys-worlds], Justin Desai, Decktech (15 October 2000). Horbey played Tennet in game 6 with an Akesson-style [[You Can Either Profit By This... / Or Be Destroyed|Profit]] list. Tennet won by about 20.<ref name="tennet" /> Olson played Snider in game 1 (Hidden Base / Tatooine Celebrating).<ref name="snider" /> Anderson drove overnight from Alabama, started late with the registration line, and stayed to watch the Final Confrontation on the big screen.<ref name="anderson-pds2" />

== Day 2 ==

After the Day 1 cut, [[Justin Pakes]] announced the places through 38. Place 39, the alternate, was [[Gabriel Alonso]].<ref name="tennet" /> Tennet wrote that he was sure Alonso would get in the next day.<ref name="tennet" /> [[Mike Kessling]] had also played Day 1 and missed the 38.<ref name="tennet" />

On Friday morning [[Michael Riboulet]], the Naboo Regional winner, had missed his flight and was not in attendance.<ref name="tennet" /><ref name="herren" /> Herren and Kessling reached the hall about 9:20 a.m. Kessling spoke with Decipher about the Naboo chair. Alonso learned of it from Kessling. After persuasion from Alonso, Decipher seated Kessling, the Naboo runner-up, and Alonso.<ref name="herren" /><ref name="tennet" />

Decipher's Day 2 results page leaves these circuit champions off the standings:<ref name="d2" /><ref name="dc00fin" />

! Circuit champion !! Event !! Day 2 seat

Decipher's formula is 32 circuit seats plus 38 wildcards. The qualifier list names 33 circuit players because Coruscant is printed with co-champions Lolli and Ziagos. Four of those named champions have no Day 2 row.

[[Mike Kessling]] filled Riboulet's chair. [[Josh Smith]] finished 2nd at [[2000 Bespin Regionals]] and finished 42nd on Day 2.<ref name="d2" /><ref name="tr-bespin-li">[[Jim Li Bespin Regional Omaha Nebraska (tournament report)]]</ref> That pairing is the editorial reading for Reisch's chair.

[[2000 Sullust Regionals]] names Chrobak as the qualifier.<ref name="dc00fin" /> [[Patrick Ziagos]] is the extra Coruscant co-champion already on the official list. The editorial reading puts that extra name in Chrobak's empty chair.

[[Jared Lockwood]] finished 2nd at [[2000 Corellia Regionals]] and won the [[2000 Wizard World Open]]. He finished 35th on Day 2 in the Open chair.<ref name="dc00fin" /><ref name="d2" /><ref name="tr-corellia-olson">[[Eric Olson Corellia Regional 5th Place 6-3-00 (tournament report)]]</ref> Corellia 3rd is unpublished. [[Gabriel Alonso]] was the Day 1 39th alternate and played Day 2. The editorial reading puts Alonso in Fred's empty chair. Fred in attendance leaves Alonso the unused 39th alternate.

Tennet, writing of Thursday night, already expected Alonso would play Day 2. Riboulet's Friday morning no-show is the chair Kessling filled.

Day 2 opened near on time, about an hour late by Winkelhaus's clock.<ref name="winkelhaus-tr" /> Eight games, four per side. Twelve advanced.

[[Clint Hays]] led the table 14 (+85). [[Kyle Craft]] was second 14 (+65). [[Martin Falke]] was third 13 (+54). Sokol finished eighth 12 (+6) on [[Jonny Chu]]'s Hidden Base X-wing Light and his own Bring Him Before Me Dark ("the beast").<ref name="d2" /><ref name="sokol-dt" /> Winkelhaus started 5–0, then lost his last three to Akesson, Craft, and Carman, and finished 22nd 9 (+42).<ref name="winkelhaus-tr" /><ref name="d2" /> Hunter finished 15th 10 (+54) after a modified loss to [[Paul Todd Feldman]] in game 8.<ref name="d2" /><ref name="hayes-tr" />

The top 12 advanced to Day 3. Places 1–57 are Final Totals from the Decipher Day 2 page. Places 58–70 are opponents in those game logs with no Final Total, ordered by fewest games skipped, then victory points, then differential. [[Team Albany]] built Sokol's Day 3 [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB Operations]] list overnight after Day 2. [[Brian Terwilliger]], [[Chris Terwilliger]], [[Jonny Chu]], [[Arthur Wright]], and [[Aaron Kingery]] sat with him on that build.<ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="sokol" /> Sokol's Light for Days 2–3 was Chu's Hidden Base X-wing swarm. Sokol later cut Luke and added inserts for the Final Confrontation.<ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="chu-pds2" />

== Final Confrontation ==

The match was played in a closed room. The audience watched on a large screen next door, with commentary by [[Joe Alread]], [[Kyle Heuer]], and [[Kendrick Summers]]. Jean-Luc Simard's Decipher report and Sokol's Decktech report are the play-by-play sources.<ref name="jls3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001117011300/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/jls3.html Matt Sokol, 2000 Star Wars CCG World Champion!], Jean-Luc Simard, Decipher (Wayback 17 November 2000)</ref><ref name="sokol-dt" /> [[Justin Pakes]] and [[Joe Helfrich]] judged.<ref name="dcon-fc-jdg">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk&t=832s DecipherCon 2000 SWCCG World Championship Final Confrontation], Player's Council (20 February 2022), 13:52–14:35. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-Q0sFxQ2i3Hk Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008004102/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 8 October 2026).</ref> [[Mark Tuttle]] called play-by-play, with color commentary by Alread.<ref name="dcon-fc-comm">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk&t=82s DecipherCon 2000 SWCCG World Championship Final Confrontation], Player's Council (20 February 2022), 1:22–1:32. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-Q0sFxQ2i3Hk Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008004102/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 8 October 2026).</ref> [[Chris Craig]] did rulings throughout the tournament.<ref name="dcon-fc-jdg" />

Game 1: Sokol [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]] (X-wings / Numbers) against Lapointe [[Bring Him Before Me / Take Your Father's Place|Bring Him Before Me]]. Sokol's Light list went in at 59 cards; he added [[Civil Disorder]] at registration and the deck had no Luke. Lapointe won by 20.<ref name="jls3" /><ref name="sokol-dt" />

Game 2: Sokol [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB Operations]] (walkers / Sandwhirl) against Lapointe's Super Falcon list. Sokol needed at least 21 Force of differential. An [[Abyssin Ornament]] left him on 25 Life Force; Lapointe drew his last card. Combined: Sokol 2 (+5), Lapointe 2 (−5).<ref name="jls3" />

Sokol later won the Sunday team constructed event with Chu and both Terwilligers.<ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="sokol" />

The Player's Council posted the original Decipher streaming video of both games.<ref name="dcon-fc">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk DecipherCon 2000 SWCCG World Championship Final Confrontation], Player's Council (20 February 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-Q0sFxQ2i3Hk Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008004102/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 8 October 2026).</ref>

[[File:DecipherCon 2000 Worlds Final still.jpg|640px|link=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk]]

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk Watch the Final Confrontation] (1 hour 21 minutes). Convention, guests, side events, and the surviving official photographs are on [[DecipherCon 2000]].

After the match, Decipher recorded a post-match interview with Sokol and Lapointe. Derek Brooks provided the footage; brandon baity (NanashiStudios) posted it on 21 August 2018.<ref name="dcon-iv">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ECUW3AIAH3A DecipherCon 2000 Championship Match Interview], brandon baity (NanashiStudios) (21 August 2018). Footage by Derek Brooks. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ECUW3AIAH3A Internet Archive].</ref>

Published constructed lists from Decipher Deck Designs and DeckTech are under [[#Day 3 decklists]]. Day 1 and Day 2 Dark and Light cells sit on those standings tables.<ref name="sokol" />

== Recollections ==

Players writing in October 2000 and speaking in later interviews treated the weekend as the Death Star II constructed peak. The expansion had been out for three months. Honor of the Jedi had already punished Hunt Down. No Escape from Enhanced Jabba's Palace was on sale at the convention and was not legal for Worlds.<ref name="ds2" /><ref name="sokol" /><ref name="hayes-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M&t=2200s SWCCG PDS2: Hayes Hunter Worlds 2023 Champion Interview], BillBisco2 (10 May 2025), 36:40–38:50. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-qJuistFFk9M Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010406/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 16 October 2026).</ref><ref name="olson-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A-yqKSMt6gE&t=2223s SWCCG PDS2: Joe Olson Interview], BillBisco2 (12 May 2025), 37:03–39:25. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-A-yqKSMt6gE Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016011720/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A-yqKSMt6gE watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 16 October 2026)</ref>

[[Hayes Hunter]] called the event "sort of a pinnacle I think of the game." Death Star II had come out in the summer. Worlds was in October. "A three-month window… but everybody remembers that time period."<ref name="hayes-pds2" /> Two weeks after the final, Sokol told Trandosite: "Death Star 2 changed the game so much. You can get so much force fast now… it is insane."<ref name="sokol" /> [[Jonny Chu]] said Hidden Base X-wings work because of Death Star II: without [[Honor Of The Jedi]], Hunt Down is hard.<ref name="chu-pds2" /> [[Joe Olson]], then 15, flew in off a Portland Grand Slam win, played last-minute Hunt Down, and "just got crushed." He said Honor of the Jedi "just like crushes Hunt Down."<ref name="olson-pds2" />

Winkelhaus told Trandosite in May 2000 that Worlds are "the biggest and best tournament every year."<ref name="trando-iv3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026204829/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv3.htm Bastian Winkelhaus interview], [[Trandosite]] (26 May 2000)</ref> After Day 2 in Kissimmee he wrote that it was a great experience.<ref name="winkelhaus-tr" /> Fitzgerald called it the biggest tournament of the year.<ref name="fitz" /> Arendt wrote that Day 1 was fierce because so many seats were open.<ref name="arendt" />

Sokol went in expecting Day 2, maybe Day 3, not a title. "What kept me going was all my friends on Team Albany."<ref name="sokol" /> Friday night Chu handed him Hidden Base X-wings. Sokol's own Light had gone 1–3 on Day 1.<ref name="sokol-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jFXqTc1jkNc&t=2707s SWCCG PDS2: Matt Sokol, Worlds 2000 Champion Interview], BillBisco2 (6 May 2025), 45:07–48:21. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-jFXqTc1jkNc Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008224620/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jFXqTc1jkNc watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 8 October 2026).</ref> After the Final Confrontation he heard friends screaming in the next room: "it was the greatest feeling in the world."<ref name="sokol" /> He later said Chu and Brian Terwilliger were the reasons he won.<ref name="sokol-pds2" /> The next day Team Albany won the team event. Sokol called it "the best weekend ever."<ref name="sokol-pds2" />

Hunter said Day 3 was a poor, anticlimactic miniature Swiss and that Sokol "totally deserved it."<ref name="hayes-pds2" /> He later said Day 1 was poorly run: first pairings went up at 1 p.m., and play ran until 2 a.m.<ref name="hayes-pds2-ops" /> [[Paul Todd Feldman]] said the tournament software was not working properly and that pairings took a long time.<ref name="feldman-pds2-ops" /> Feldman called the weekend "a cluster" and said 2000 "looked like a company that wanted to go bankrupt."<ref name="feldman-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I&t=5014s SWCCG PDS2: Paul Todd Feldman Interview], BillBisco2 (29 May 2025), 1:23:34–1:27:26. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-b9f9tNBiU2I Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261014143045/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 14 October 2026)</ref> He finished 11th on Day 3 and then stopped playing.<ref name="feldman-pds2" /> Hunter said that after a game finished, players talked about what the opponent had played. He named [[Team Albany]], [[Clint Hays|Clinton]], and [[Steven Lewis]], and a warning such as "watch out, he has a copy of [[Lost In The Wilderness]]."<ref name="hayes-pds2-scout">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M&t=3043s SWCCG PDS2: Hayes Hunter Worlds 2023 Champion Interview], BillBisco2 (10 May 2025), 50:43–51:20. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-qJuistFFk9M Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010406/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 16 October 2026).</ref> Olson said players with teams had a huge advantage, and that Sokol won because Team Albany worked together.<ref name="olson-pds2" />

[[Jeff Anderson]] played his only Decipher Worlds that weekend. He finished 86th on Day 1, missed the cut on differential, and watched Sokol versus Lapointe on the big screen with 25–30 people.<ref name="anderson-pds2" /> [[Steven Lewis]], after the Day 1 disqualification, wrote that he played so he could meet people from around the world. "Did I do that at Worlds? ABSOLUTELY!"<ref name="lewis" />

== Discrepancies ==

Where a source disagrees with the record on this page, the page keeps the record and notes the difference here.

* Decipher's qualifier formula is 1 defending champion + 4 Open + 3 Continental + 24 Regional + 38 wildcards = 70 World Finalists. The official list names 33 circuit players because Coruscant is printed with co-champions. Four named champions have no Day 2 row: [[Brian Fred]], [[Michael Riboulet]], [[Leszek Chrobak]], and [[Nick Reisch]]. [[Mike Kessling]] filled Riboulet's chair. [[Josh Smith]] is the editorial reading for Reisch's chair. [[Patrick Ziagos]] is the extra co-champion on the official list; the editorial reading puts that name in Chrobak's empty chair. [[Gabriel Alonso]] is the Day 1 39th alternate; the editorial reading puts him in Fred's empty chair. [[Jared Lockwood]] already held the Wizard World Open chair. [[2000 Sullust Regionals]] names Chrobak as the qualifier.<ref name="dc00fin" /><ref name="d2" /><ref name="tennet" /><ref name="herren" /><ref name="tr-bespin-li" /><ref name="tr-corellia-olson" />
* Decipher's 2000 Regionals listing names [[Bert-Olof Lundin]] as the Toola qualifier; the official Worlds qualifier list and Day 2 standings name [[Jesper Larsson]]. Akesson wrote that Larsson won the Toola final. The Qualifiers table follows the Worlds list.<ref name="rl00toola" /><ref name="dc00fin" /><ref name="d2" /><ref name="tr-d1133" />
* Snider describes four Day 2 games (0 (−22) after game 1, 0 (−43) after game 2, then two more losses before dropping); Decipher's Day 2 page has him on 0 (−38) with five of eight games missed, i.e. three played, and the hub summarises his Day 2 as 0–2.<ref name="tr-d1309" />
* Guzman counts 170 players on Day 1. Wikipedia and Star Wars Insider 52 give 72. Lalumiere's Decipher floor report also gives 170. The Field line lists about 170 as the open and 72 as the Wikipedia / Insider figure.<ref name="tr-d1317">[[Tim Guzman Info Broker's DCon Day One Report (tournament report)]]</ref>
* Herren gives his Day 2 total as 8 (+18) (his eight margins add to +18); Decipher's Day 2 page lists him 26th with 8 (17).<ref name="tr-d1322">[[Charlie Herren The Bad Player Goes to DecipherCon (tournament report)]]</ref>
* Gaudreault writes that Alex Klammrodt 'did 3-4 drop' on Day 2, but the Decipher Day 2 log on the hub gives Klammrodt 4 (−10) with 2 of 8 games missed, i.e. 2–4.<ref name="tr-d1333">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-12-dom-goes-to-floridad1333/ dom-goes-to-florida], DeckTech (Dominic "Decktech" Gaudreault, 12 October 2000). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-12-dom-goes-to-floridad1333/ GitHub Pages].</ref>
* Doug Faust, on the Day 1 staff, wrote that Peter Di Biasio won Day 1 and Dominic Gaudreault was 2nd; the hub gives Bastian Winkelhaus 2nd (7–1), Hayes Hunter 3rd and Gaudreault 4th from the players' own reports.<ref name="tr-d1335">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-12-deciphercon-2kd1335/ deciphercon-2k], DeckTech (Doug "Phrim" Faust, 12 October 2000). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-12-deciphercon-2kd1335/ GitHub Pages].</ref>
* Faust, who helped enter the command cards, gives 170 Day 1 players. The Field line lists about 170 from Lalumiere, Guzman and Faust, and 72 from Wikipedia and Insider 52.<ref name="tr-d1335" />
* Tennet writes that Sokol won Final game 2 by 21 after losing game 1 by 20; the hub's combined score 2 (+5) implies a game 2 margin of 25.<ref name="tr-d1338" />
* Winkelhaus thinks Gary Carman finished Day 2 "9th or 10th"; the hub (Decipher Day 2 page) has Carman 11th, 10 (+99).<ref name="tr-d1340">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-deciphercon-by-bastian-winkelhausd1340/ deciphercon-by-bastian-winkelhaus], DeckTech (Bastian "Death Star" Winkelhaus, 14 October 2000). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-deciphercon-by-bastian-winkelhausd1340/ GitHub Pages].</ref>
* The hub says Steven Lewis was 3–0 after game 3 when he was disqualified; Lewis's own report gives 2–1, 4 (+43): he won games 1 and 3 and lost game 2 to Adam Weinstein.<ref name="tr-d1349">[[Steven Lewis How to Get Disqualified at Worlds (tournament report)]]</ref>
* Klema finished "60 something" and his roommate Jeremy Oakes 100th on Day 1, which does not fit a 72-player Day 1 field (Wikipedia / Insider 52); it fits the 170 reported by Lalumiere, Guzman and Faust. Oakes sits in the Day 1 table at 100.<ref name="tr-d1356">[[Andy Klema RexBanner Goes to D-Con (tournament report)]]</ref>
* Hays gives his Day 2 total as 14 (+89 'i think'); the hub (Decipher Day 2 Final Totals) has 14 (+85).<ref name="tr-d1409">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-31-deciphercon-p-e-n-i-sd1409/ deciphercon-p-e-n-i-s], DeckTech (Clint "GameMaster" Hays, 31 October 2000). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-31-deciphercon-p-e-n-i-sd1409/ GitHub Pages].</ref>
* Hays's Day 3 running totals (−24, then −17, then about −45, then a win by about 25) end near −37 and he writes '4(-lots)'; the hub (Decipher Day 3 page) has 4 (−17).<ref name="tr-d1409" />
